primitives.name: AWS Cost Optimization Primitive
primitives.verbatim_quote: | cost worksheet, cap, kill switch | estimated monthly cost, variable-cost driver count | Cost, Budgets, Cost Explorer | require zero default and owner cap | billing owner | | Sustainability | Can the system avoid unnecessary compute and storage?
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'C_{\\text{cap}}': 'Total fixed cost ceiling (USD/month)', 'C_{\\text{budget}}(t)': 'Time-varying budget allocation function (USD/month)', 't': 'Time index (months)'}
primitives.assumptions: Constant USD exchange rate, linear scaling, no hidden charges.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Variable-cost drivers exceed threshold -> non-negligible noise.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE resource-allocation duality: maximize utility U subject to cost constraint C ≤ B, where B is the 'kill switch' budget.
layer2.telemetry: Actual vs. projected spend variance (USD) and driver-count change rate.

primitives.name: AWS Reliability Test Primitive
primitives.verbatim_quote: | fixture replay, fallback plan, no-action gate | fallback coverage, stale-source rejection rate | EC2/compute, networking | add local failure-mode table | production owner | | Performance efficiency | Is managed infrastructure needed yet?
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_f': 'Failure-rejection reliability (dimensionless, 0 to 1)', 'N_{\\text{stale}}': 'Stale-source rejection count', 'N_{\\text{total}}': 'Total failure attempts'}
primitives.assumptions: Deterministic failure injection, no race conditions.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE state-transition logic: model system as finite-state machine M with transition relation δ, verify that all transitions lead to safe states S_{\text{safe}}.
layer2.telemetry: Replay success rate and average manual intervention steps.

primitives.assumptions: Constant data generation, negligible processing delay.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI operational-excellence duality: maximize throughput Θ while minimizing latency L, subject to capacity constraints.
layer2.telemetry: Runtime percentiles (P95, P99) and queue depth spikes.
